raw_plan.interpretation: Create one acquisition email in English for Dutch municipalities whose web teams need privacy-friendly analytics that does not depend on visitor consent. The reader relationship is unknown, so the email will not assume the municipality currently uses GA4 or has failed a compliance scan. intent.reason_now: Municipal websites may be scrutinized for loading third-party services before consent, while public bodies cannot make access conditional on cookie consent.
intent.desired_action: Book a demo to discuss the municipality's analytics setup and a 30-day proof of concept.

raw_plan.reader: A Dutch municipal web, analytics or privacy team considering how to retain useful website statistics without making measurement depend on visitor consent.
raw_plan.reader_segment: A Dutch or EU public-sector web team told its site may not load Google before consent, and that a public body cannot use a cookie wall
raw_plan.reader_scope: Dutch municipalities only; do not generalize the proposition to every EU public-sector organization.
raw_plan.promise: A municipality can measure how people find and browse its website without making the analytics script depend on visitor consent, then evaluate the approach alongside its current setup before deciding whether to switch.
raw_plan.orientation: Simple Analytics is a cookieless, EU-hosted website analytics tool that records useful traffic information without collecting personal data or identifying visitors.
raw_plan.arc: In one self-contained email, move the reader from treating consent-dependent measurement as unavoidable to seeing a concrete, low-disruption way to evaluate cookieless analytics alongside the current setup.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: The audience is already solution-aware, so the email should open with the operational outcome—useful statistics when consent is rejected—rather than explaining cookie compliance at length. The no-cookie mechanism and retained visibility supply the reason to consider Simple Analytics; the assisted 30-day proof of concept answers the practical hesitation about changing analytics before privacy and reporting stakeholders can compare results. One email is sufficient because the requested deliverable has one slot, and the proposition, mechanism, qualification and next step can stand alone.
